text:
Ashley: seeing a sharp p95 hop increase between gpu-node-3a -> gpu-node-7b in rack-9 during the 12:20 batching window. latency jumped from ~6ms to ~180-220ms for ~3 mins. RDMA retries and a bunch of QP errors in dmesg. anyone else?
Mike: ack. i see pings between those hosts spike and a handful of TCP retransmits. not global across the rack, seems to be that podset.
Tara: grabbing logs. infra-bot do we have recent config changes pushed to rack-9?
infra-bot: deploy: net-qos-policy update applied to rack-9 at 11:58 by infra-ci. Change ID: net-qos-2026-11.
Ashley: that could line up. tcpdump sample from gpu-node-7b during spike (filtered):
```
12:21:14.123456 IP 10.4.7.3 > 10.4.3.7: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12400, ack 54321, win 65535, length 55
12:21:14.303789 IP 10.4.7.3 > 10.4.3.7: tcp retransmission
```
Mike: ibv_devinfo on node7 shows some port counters increasing: "port_xmit_discards" and "port_rcv_errors". ethtool -S on mlx5 shows "tx_queue_drops" bump.
Ivan: interesting — could be MTU mismatch or jumbo negotiation failing on the east-west path. can you check if any TOR changes rolled?
Tara: no TOR pushes in last 24h per infra-bot. but QoS policy touched TC qdiscs on host interfaces.
Sophia: can we confirm MTU on both endpoints?
Ashley: checked: both nodes show 9000 on ifconfig. but on a failing trace the inner IP packet shows 1500 sized fragments (we're VXLAN-ing). suspect VXLAN tunnel MTU reduction during high batch coalescing.
Jamie: also saw RDMA QP reset events in journal: "mlx5_core: QP 0x7a reset due to retry_timeout" around same time.
Mike: quick mitigation: lowered batching concurrency for that fleet to reduce packet sizes and retried — p95 dropped back to ~12ms. but that's a blunt lever.
Tara: can we try toggling GRO/GSO off on the VXLAN interface temporarily to see if it stabilizes? small test first on node7b.
Ashley: doing it now: `ip link set dev vxlan100 gro off gso off`
Ashley: immediate improvement noted, p95 down to ~14ms within 30s. TCP retransmits stopped.
Ivan: that’s consistent with an offload/fragmentation edge case in the NIC tunneling path. likely vendor driver bug with large coalesced frames + VXLAN + RDMA.
Sophia: next steps: roll this test to a subset of nodes in rack-9 (canary 10%) and monitor. open vendor ticket with driver + firmware + kernel ring buffer.
Jamie: logging vendor data: ethtool -i, firmware version, mlx5 logs, full tcpdump capture with non-truncated packets. I'll collect and upload to ticket.
Ashley: created quick incident note in incidents channel and flagged oncall. if canary looks good we'll push a temporary QoS rollback or host GRO disable across the rack for the next 6 hours.
Mike: also adding a metric to alert on concurrent QP resets + vxlan tx drops so we catch earlier.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-447. Priority: P2.
Tara: documenting runbook steps: 1) identify affected node pairs; 2) reduce batch concurrency to 50% if immediate relief needed; 3) disable GRO/GSO on vxlan interface; 4) gather vendor artifacts; 5) schedule firmware/driver patch with vendor.
Sophia: noted. i'll own vendor comms.
Ashley: thanks all — keeping this thread updated as canary rolls. :thumbsup:
Mike: nice catch. good to have the quick host-level mitigation available.
Ivan: follow-up: we should also add a preflight check to the rollout pipeline to validate VXLAN MTU headroom when changing QoS or qdisc configs.
Ashley: agreed, adding to infra backlog.
Jamie: uploading artifacts now to INC-2026-447.
infra-bot: update: canary (rack-9 subset) with GRO off shows stable p95 for 20m. Monitoring continues.
